content.user_title: Analyze Discount Leakage With Pocket-Price Waterfalls
content.value_statement: Discounts, rebates, and credits can obscure the difference between list price and realized revenue. This workflow structures customer-level analysis and turns major deductions into policy recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Defines customer data requirements, including list price, billing cadence, discount reasons, payment terms, implementation fees, and credits.
Outlines waterfall deductions for ramp, volume, bundle, prepayment, strategic, promotional, rebate, credit, payment-term, and implementation concessions.
Provides diagnostic questions about deduction size, commercial value, approval controls, revenue exposure, and segment differences.
Structures customer and cohort findings into a report with ranked deductions and three priority policies.
Guides policy drafting with approval thresholds, required concessions, documentation requirements, and accepted reason codes.
Provides a recovery-estimation formula using discount-rate changes and affected cohort revenue.
limitations: The referenced Python calculator is absent from the reviewed package, so automated calculations cannot be verified or run from this package alone.
The referenced pricing framework and sibling review skills are outside the reviewed package.
Requires operator-provided customer data; no CRM or billing connector is included.
Recovery estimates depend on assumptions and do not guarantee revenue or profit improvements.

use_cases.title: Assess Revenue Deductions
use_cases.description: Review customer discount and credit data to distinguish list prices from realized prices and identify major deductions.

use_cases.title: Draft Discount Approval Policies
use_cases.description: Translate discretionary concessions into approval thresholds, required commercial exchanges, and standardized reason codes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Cohort Pricing Reviews
use_cases.description: Compare discount patterns across customer segments and prepare conservative recovery scenarios for a quarterly pricing review.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Required Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these available pricing fields: [fields]. List missing inputs needed for a pocket-price waterfall. Do not invent customer values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a customer pricing dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Customer Waterfall
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [customer data], show deductions from annual list price to pocket price. State assumptions and missing values. Do not claim the absent calculator ran.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: analyze a customer with supplied amounts.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Discount Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [discount findings] and [approval constraints]. Draft policies for deductions exceeding 5% of revenue. Include approval thresholds, required concessions, documentation, and reason codes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert findings into approval controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review Cohort Recovery Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [cohort data], rank the three largest deductions and compare segments. Estimate conservative recovery from [proposed discount changes]. State revenue bases, assumptions, and missing dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a cohort review with recovery estimates.

output_examples.input: Annual list price is $1,000. Ramp discount is $100, volume discount is $50, and credits total $20. No other deductions apply.
output: Illustrative pocket price: $830 per customer per year.
Total deduction from list price: $170, or 17%.
Policy review priority: verify the ramp discount duration and required commercial concession.

output_examples.input: Strategic discounts average 12% of a $500,000 annual list-price revenue base. A proposed policy targets 8% without changing customer volume.
output: Illustrative annual recovery: $20,000, calculated as a four-percentage-point reduction multiplied by $500,000.
Required assumptions: unchanged revenue base, customer retention, and other deductions.
Policy draft: require manager approval above 8% and record the commercial concession for each exception.
This is a scenario estimate, not a guaranteed result or verified calculator output.

best_practices: Normalize billing cadence and distinguish percentage discounts from dollar deductions before comparing customers.
Record missing data and inspect any separately obtained calculator before executing it with customer information.
Use conservative recovery assumptions and connect approval thresholds to documented commercial concessions.
anti_patterns: Treating list price as realized revenue while ignoring rebates, credits, or payment-term costs.
Reporting successful script execution when the calculator is missing or its output is unavailable.
Presenting a projected discount reduction as guaranteed recovery without retention and revenue-base assumptions.

faq.question: What is a pocket-price waterfall?
faq.answer: It traces deductions from list price to pocket price, including discounts, rebates, credits, payment-term costs, and implementation concessions.

faq.question: Which customer inputs are needed?
faq.answer: Provide list prices, billing cadence, discount amounts and reasons, payment terms, implementation fees, and credits for each customer.

faq.question: Is the Python calculator included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only instructions. Obtain and inspect the referenced calculator separately before using its documented command.

faq.question: Does this skill retrieve CRM data?
faq.answer: No connector is included. The operator must provide the data or export it from authorized CRM and billing systems.

faq.question: What policy recommendations does it structure?
faq.answer: It structures approval thresholds, required commercial concessions, documentation rules, accepted reason codes, and forbidden discount reasons.

faq.question: Are recovery estimates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Estimates depend on discount changes, affected revenue, customer retention, and other assumptions. Validate these assumptions before changing policy.
